title: Pydantic v2: validating external data

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?

Pydantic was created by Samuel Colvin to make parsing and validating external data with Python types practical. In v2, `BaseModel` defines the schema and `Field` adds constraints; treat `ValidationError` as an expected input failure. Type hints alone do not validate at runtime, and Pydantic does not replace authorization or business rules.

CORE EXPLANATION

Python type hints help readers and static analysis, but do not validate incoming JSON at runtime. Pydantic v2 models parse external dictionaries or JSON into typed values and enforce declared constraints. Use
BaseModel
Field
, and
model_validate()
; invalid input raises
ValidationError
. Validation does not establish trust or replace authorization and business rules.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Install Pydantic v2 in the active virtual environment with `python -m pip install 'pydantic>=2,<3'` and pin the version in the project.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Map validation errors to safe user-facing responses and never log secrets. Pydantic v1 examples do not use the same API as v2.

PRACTICE EXAMPLE 3 · Pydantic v2: validating external data
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Account(BaseModel):
    username: str = Field(min_length=3)

account = Account.model_validate({'username': 'ada'})
print(account.model_dump())
